theorem: If a randomized adaptive verifier accepts a hard assignment y with probability greater than the soundness bound beta for non-hard assignments, then the union of variables queried on accepting executions at y is a deterministic 1-certificate.
formula_consequence: The accepting-union polarity classes for HardF satisfy the same two-sided formula-footprint lower bound as deterministic certificates.
proof_dependencies: adaptive path invariance under assignments agreeing on all queried variables
boundary: does not lower-bound expected query count
does not handle arbitrary interactive communication-query product
remaining_open_problem: expected-footprint or information-theoretic randomized certificate lower bound
